parts.latex:
A ten-sided die has faces numbered 1 to 10.

The die is constructed so that the probability of obtaining the number 1 is greater than the probability of obtaining any of the other numbers. The numbers 2 to 10 are equally likely to occur.

When the die is rolled 153 times, a 1 is obtained 72 times.

By using the relative frequency of rolling a 1, which of the following is the best estimate for the probability of rolling a 10?

solutions.latex:
Using relative frequency:
$$P(1)\approx\dfrac{72}{153}=\dfrac{8}{17}$$
The remaining probability is shared equally by the 9 numbers 2 to 10:
$$\begin{aligned} P(10) &= \dfrac{1}{9}\left(1-\dfrac{8}{17}\right) \\ &= \dfrac{1}{9}\times\dfrac{9}{17} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{17} \end{aligned}$$

If a tree is randomly selected, find the probability the height is less than $1.25$ m but not less than $0.45$ m.

solutions.latex:
Each frequency is the difference of consecutive cumulative frequencies, and the cumulative frequencies are running totals.

\extable{Ts3105_1}
criteria: $3$ values correct, or $3$ values correct that follow from a previous error

meta.top_criterion_original: 2 for all correct; 1 for 3 correct, or 3 correct that follow from a previous error
meta.format_note: Table values checked: frequencies 2, 6, 7, 11, 14, 3 total 43, matching the cumulative column 2, 8, 15, 26, 40, 43.

solutions.latex:
The modal class has the highest frequency, $14$.
$$\text{Modal class: } 1.7\text{-}2.0 \text{ m}$$

The heights from $0.45$ m up to $1.25$ m are the trees with height less than $1.25$ m, minus those less than $0.45$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= \dfrac{15-2}{43} \\ &= \dfrac{13}{43} \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, the classes $0.5\text{-}0.8$ and $0.9\text{-}1.2$ have frequencies $6$ and $7$:
$$P=\dfrac{6+7}{43}=\dfrac{13}{43}$$

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.latex: Median: changes; mean: stays the same

options.label: D

parts.latex:
Consider the following data set.

$4\quad 7\quad 7\quad 9\quad 12\quad 15$

Which row of the table shows how the median and mean are affected when a score of 9 is added to the data set?

solutions.latex:
Original data set (6 scores): the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th scores.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{median} &= \dfrac{7+9}{2} = 8 \\ \text{mean} &= \dfrac{4+7+7+9+12+15}{6} = \dfrac{54}{6} = 9 \end{aligned}$$
Add a score of 9: the data set is $4,\ 7,\ 7,\ 9,\ 9,\ 12,\ 15$ (7 scores), so the median is the 4th score.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{median} &= 9 \\ \text{mean} &= \dfrac{54+9}{7} = \dfrac{63}{7} = 9 \end{aligned}$$
The median changes from $8$ to $9$, and the mean stays at $9$ (adding a score equal to the mean does not change the mean).

Therefore the row is: median changes, mean stays the same.

2595.stem:
The cumulative frequency graph, published by DAHTAH, shows the distribution of the number of app downloads made by 100 people in an hour.

\exfigure{1037_q11_1}

figures.cap: cumulative frequency histogram and ogive of number of downloads

parts.latex: Find the interquartile range for the number of downloads.
parts.note: Interquartile range from a cumulative frequency graph (IQR is Standard statistics).

parts.latex: What is the mode for the number of downloads?

One minute, after representing the data on the graph, it was reported that 15 people made 10 downloads during that hour. This piece of data was delayed due to a technical glitch. If this new set of data is an outlier then DAHTAH will not update the graph. Otherwise, the graph has to be updated to include this piece of information.

Does DAHTAH need to update the graph to include this latest piece of information? Show your mathematical reasoning.
parts.note: Outlier test using IQR fences (Standard statistics).

solutions.latex:
From the cumulative frequency graph:
$$Q_1=16,\quad Q_3=20$$
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= Q_3-Q_1 \\ &= 20-16 \\ &= 4 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds either $Q_1$ or $Q_3$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The mode is where the cumulative frequency graph rises most steeply (the greatest increase).
$$\text{Mode}=20$$

A value is an outlier if it is below $Q_1-1.5\times IQR$.
$$\begin{aligned} Q_1-1.5\times IQR &= 16-1.5\times 4 \\ &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
The value 10 is not below the lower fence, so it is not an outlier.

Therefore the graph needs updating.
criteria: Calculates the lower fence, or equivalent merit
